style: Use the language liberally and don't translate right away. Favor vocabulary and idioms over grammar drills.

difficulty.word_order: Subject-verb-object like English. Object pronouns go before the verb.
difficulty.noun_cases: None. Nouns carry gender and number only.
difficulty.new_sounds: Double consonants, rolled r, gli, gn.
difficulty.closest_known: English shares much Latin vocabulary. Spanish is very close.

common.english: here it is / there you go

essentials.questions_negatives: Questions keep statement word order; rising intonation makes the question. Negate with 'non' before the verb.
patterns: Subject pronouns are usually dropped; the verb ending carries the person.
Adjectives usually follow the noun and agree in gender and number.
With piacere the thing liked is the subject: mi piace la pizza.
Past tense is avere/essere + past participle.
